name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male Levite who served as a chief officer among the Levites, indicating a leadership role within the tribe dedicated to priestly and temple duties. He was the son of Kemuel, and his position suggests he was likely a descendant of Aaron, the first high priest. His role underscores the organized structure of Levitical service during the time recorded in 1 Chronicles.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'YHWH has reckoned,' reflecting a theologically rich Hebrew name that acknowledges God's sovereignty. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 27:17, was not given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine accounting or judgment.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hashabiah as the son of Kemuel, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, there are no additional family relationships recorded for him in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's significance lies in his leadership role among the Levites, serving as a chief officer, which implies responsibility over the tribe's duties related to worship and temple service. His likely descent from Aaron connects him to the priestly lineage entrusted with maintaining covenantal worship. This highlights the structured governance of the Levitical tribe during the period chronicled, emphasizing faithfulness to God's ordained order.
